What did the FBI investigate in 1947?.answer:
There are 33 FBI records from 1947; eight are shown here. They concern reports of flying discs and other unusual objects, including the June 24 Mount Rainier/Mount Adams reports [1947-FBI-0292] [1947-FBI-33B6], sightings near Bakersfield, Boise, Hackensack, and Twin Falls [1947-FBI-22AF] [1947-FBI-3A2E52] [1947-FBI-0E20EB] [1947-FBI-1E3E2B], and photographs taken in Phoenix [1947-FBI-54799C].

The FBI and Navy also examined a reported disc that landed on a Seattle roof. They found a constructed device made with plywood, radio tubes, and an oil container [1947-FBI-589206]. Several of the other reports remain unresolved in the records shown.

Which incidents involved radar detection.answer:
Thirty-three records mention radar. The incidents described in the records shown are:

- January 1947, North Sea: Radar detected a fast object that an RAF fighter could not intercept. [1947-USN-7828E5]
- April 18, 1948: Air-search radar tracked a target; its location is not stated. [1948-USAF-A09FD8]
- March 1–4, 1950, Oak Ridge: Stuart Adcock reported repeated radar returns. Investigators could not verify them and questioned his equipment’s reliability. [1950-USAF-ABC2] [1950-USAF-3455]
- June 29, 1950, Phoenix: An object seen by witnesses was also tracked by radar and pursued by a B-29. [1950-USAF-B40F]
- October 12, 1950, Oak Ridge: Ground radar indicated at least eleven objects. An intercepting fighter reported no visual or onboard-radar contact. [1950-USAF-A022]
- December 14, 1950, Oak Ridge: Radar showed a group of targets; a fighter intercept produced no visual identification. [1950-USAF-0972]
- December 20, 1950, Oak Ridge: Radar detected a slow-moving return. An F-82 intercepted and circled a small smoke cloud. [1950-USAF-1E05]
- July 1955, near Newfoundland: A KC-97 crew’s sighting coincided with ground-radar returns. A USAF committee could not explain both, according to DOW-UAP-D095, Joint U.S.-Canadian Aviation Projects and UFO Sighting Reports, 1954-1955.
- November 19, 1964, near Puerto Rico: A Navy pilot reported an object, and USS Gyatt recorded a radar track. CIA-UAP-D022, Unidentified Flying Object Reported near Puerto Rico, 1965, and CIA-UAP-D023, Briefing Notes for Mr. Walter Elder, describe the same incident.

What happened near Washington D.C.?.answer:
Several reports concerned Washington, D.C. In 1950, a resident reported a high-altitude, silvery, cigar-shaped object moving east; the case remained unresolved [1950-FBI-6552].

Records describing July 1951 say radar operators and commercial pilots observed unidentified objects over Washington for about six hours. A later radar report says jets were dispatched; one pilot saw lights that disappeared as he approached. Both cases remained unresolved [UNDATED-USAF-F28F86] [UNDATED-USAF-D173A2].

In 1952, a couple noticed an unexplained spot in a photograph taken near the Smithsonian. They had seen nothing unusual when they took it, and the case had insufficient data [1952-FBI-4C50B6].

Are there any NASA-related sightings?.answer:
Yes. There are 31 NASA records; eight are shown here. During Gemini 7, astronauts reported a “bogey” and hundreds of particles. The case identifies the bogey as debris or particles [1965-NASA-EE52BC]. The account appears in NASA-UAP-D003, Gemini 7 Transcript, 1965.

NASA-UAP-D004, Apollo 11 Technical Crew Debriefing, 1969 describes an object seen on the way to the Moon; the crew speculated it might be a rocket stage. During Apollo 12, an astronaut reported flashes and particles of light that seemed to sail into space [1969-NASA-E575D5].
